conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a potential ~1.5% monthly return, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentrates on broad market and quality names. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to address concentration and its below-stop status.
Reduce exposure to all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL, PLTU) to small positions.
This reduces overall portfolio leverage and concentration towards a more balanced risk profile.
The plan maintains some exposure to tech and semiconductors while de-risking.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for a potential ~2.5% monthly return, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while maintaining exposure to quality tech and broad indices. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a balanced growth outlook.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to address concentration and its below-stop status.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL, PLTU) to 6% each.
This strategy leans into higher-beta assets for aggressive growth potential.
Strict stop discipline is crucial given the amplified risk and daily decay of leveraged ETFs.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets a potential ~4% monthly return, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs, which amplifies both upside and drawdown potential. Be aware of the daily decay and rebalancing effects of leveraged ETFs, and the potential for substantial losses if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% for enhanced income generation, despite its below-stop status.
Add to SPY to 20% for broad market exposure and stability, despite scanner sell flag.
Sell all leveraged and high-beta single names (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL, PLTU) to zero.

income.read: This income plan targets a potential ~1% monthly return, focusing on parking cash for yield. It emphasizes income-generating ETFs and broad market exposure while eliminating leveraged and high-beta holdings. While aiming for reliable distributions, NAV can still fall in a selloff, and distributions are variable.
